To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a functional analysis of aberrant behavior is a useful tool for identifying the maintaining reinforcers for the aberrant behavior, and the results of a functional analysis can be used to develop a treatment plan that leads to a significant reduction in aberrant behaviors.

functional analyses of aberrant behavior were successful for 100% of participants in identifying maintaining variables for aberrant behavior and that the interventions developed on the basis of the functional analyses resulted in an average of an 80% reduction in aberrant behaviors in 10 days.

functional analyses conducted during short-term inpatient evaluations were successful for 100% of the participants with developmental disabilities, 96% of participants with mental retardation, and 93% of participants without developmental disabilities in identifying maintaining reinforcer(s) for aberrant behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a comprehensive assessment and treatment program for the evaluation of aberrant behavior.

the identification of the function of aberrant behavior, the development and evaluation of treatments based on the results of the assessment, and the dissemination of this information through the development and evaluation, in a variety of settings, of procedures that can be used to teach caregivers to implement behavioral treatments for aberrant behavior.
the development of a comprehensive, empirically based, and individualized treatment for children and adolescents with severe emotional disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the short-term inpatient treatment model is an effective treatment approach for the evaluation and treatment of aberrant behaviors.
the use of a functional analysis to identify the variables that are maintaining aberrant behavior and to design and implement an effective intervention is a very effective procedure.
a short-term in-patient evaluation is an appropriate method for evaluating and treating aberrant behaviors for a wide range of individuals with and without developmental disabilties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the functional analyses are successful and that the treatment is effective.

the functional analyses we conducted in the inpatient environment were successful for the vast majority of participants and resulted in a significant reduction of aberrant behavior for a majority of participants.

the short-term inpatient approach to evaluating aberrant behaviors has been successful in identifying the functions of aberrant behavior for most of the participants and in reducing aberrant behavior to acceptable levels in the majority of the participants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of functional analysis procedures to identify and treat aberrant behavior in the home is not a new idea.
functional analyses are a powerful tool for identifying and changing aberrant behavior.
functional assessment and treatment can be successfully applied in a wide range of settings and for a wide range of individuals.
